To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the activation of lymphocytes by thrombin or plasmin is accompanied by an increase in intracellular levels of cGMP.

the treatment of lymphocytes with the mitogenic concentrations of plasmin or thrombin leads to an increase in the intracellular amount cGMP, and this increase is associated with an enhancement of DNA synthesis.
the activation of lymphocytes with proteolytic enzymes leads to the enhancement of DNA synthesis and an increase of intracellular cGMP level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of proteolytic enzyme treatment on the intracellular cyclic nucleotide levels in lymphocytes and the effect on the DNA synthesis in the cells.
the study of the effect of the proteolytic enzymes thrombin and plasm on the intracellular cyclic nucleotide levels in lymphocytes and on the lymphocyte proliferative response.
the study of the effects of proteolytic agents on lymphocytes and their subpopulations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proteases are involved in the regulation of the intracellular cGMP and cAMP levels in lymphocytes and in the stimulation of the DNA synthesis.
thrombin and plasm induced proliferation of lymphocytes is realized by cAMP and cGMP dependent mechanisms.
cGMP is a second messenger for the activation of lymphocytes by proteolytic enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proteolytic enzymes, thrombin and plasmim, induce a cGMP-dependent activation of DNA synthesis in mouse spleen lymphoid cells.
the proteolytic enzyme-induced proliferation of lymphocyte cells is realized by the cAMP- and cGMP-dependent mechanism.
the proteolytic enzymes, thrombin and plasm, are mitogens for lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of proteolytic enzyme-based therapeutics should be carefully considered in patients with cardiovascular disease, particularly in patients who may have a predisposition to thrombosis.
proteases can be used to control the activity of the cell cycle and cell proliferation.
the protease thrombin is able to stimulate the proliferation of lymphocytes, and the activation of the cGMP system in the cell is the initial step in this process.
